# Limp in children

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Pediatrics > Pediatric orthopedics and trauma > Limp in children*

[Original Article Link](/library/ku0mr3)

---

## Summary

Limp is a deviation from the normal age-appropriate gait pattern. Causes range from benign conditions (e.g., <u>soft tissue</u> trauma, <u>transient synovitis</u>) to orthopedic emergencies and serious medical conditions (e.g., <u>septic arthritis</u>, <u>unstable slipped capital femoral epiphysis</u>, <u>malignancy</u>, <u>physical child abuse</u>). Clinical features vary. The patient's age and symptom duration can help determine the most likely cause. The presence of <u>red flag features</u> (e.g., inability to bear weight, <u>constitutional symptoms</u>, nocturnal <u>pain</u>) suggests a serious and/or emergent underlying cause. Evaluation begins with a thorough history and <u>physical examination</u>. Further workup may include <u>laboratory studies</u> (e.g., <u>inflammatory markers</u>, <u>synovial fluid analysis</u>) and/or imaging. Management is based on the underlying cause.
